-/

python3 - <<'E'
s=open('combi_brualdi_ch11_5.lean').read()
p='''by
  by_contra hc
  push_neg at hc
  have key : ∀ (t : Finset ℕ), t.card < n → (∀ v, G.degree v ∈ t) → False := by
    intro t ht hm
    obtain ⟨a, _, b, _, hab, h⟩ := Finset.exists_ne_map_eq_of_card_lt_of_maps_to
      (s := (Finset.univ : Finset (Fin n))) (t := t) (by simpa using ht) (f := fun v => G.degree v) (by intro v _; exact hm v)
    exact hc a b hab h
  by_cases h0 : ∃ u, G.degree u = 0
  · obtain ⟨u, hu⟩ := h0
    apply key (Finset.range (n-1)) (by simp; omega)
    intro v
    simp only [Finset.mem_range]
    by_cases hv : v = u
    · subst hv; omega
    · have hsub : G.neighborFinset v ⊆ (Finset.univ \ {v, u}) := by
        intro w hw
        rw [SimpleGraph.mem_neighborFinset] at hw
        simp only [Finset.mem_sdiff, Finset.mem_univ, Finset.mem_insert, Finset.mem_singleton, true_and, not_or]

        rintro rfl
        have : v ∈ G.neighborFinset w := by simpa using hw.symm
        have := Finset.card_pos.mpr ⟨v, this⟩
        rw [SimpleGraph.card_neighborFinset_eq_degree] at this

      omega

    apply key (Finset.Icc 1 (n-1)) (by simp; omega)
    intro v
    have := G.degree_lt_card_verts v
    simp at this
    simp only [Finset.mem_Icc]
    have := h0 v

`/work/combi_brualdi_ch11_5.lean` now compiles with no errors, and the `sorry` is replaced by a full proof. Lean still prints a deprecation warning for `push_neg`, which I left as is. I didn't change the imports or the theorem statement.

The proof is by contradiction with the pigeonhole principle. Assume all `n` vertices have different degrees. Then:

- **Some vertex has degree 0:** every other vertex `v` has no edge to it. So `v`'s neighbours lie among the `n - 2` vertices other than `v` and that one. Every degree is therefore in `{0, …, n-2}`, which has only `n - 1` values.
- **No vertex has degree 0:** every degree is at least 1 and at most `n - 1`. So all degrees lie in `{1, …, n-1}`, which again has only `n - 1` values.

Either way, `n` vertices map into a set of size `n - 1`, so two of them share a degree.
